about: The X-ray's stand view (/xray/): for each company and each of its situations, three short lines a visitor can read from a metre away in a few seconds. Each line is at most 8 words and says no more than that situation's data/xray/<slug>/xray.json (reach, mandate, gap). The 'asked' line is our example, not the company's own rules.

u1.reach: Your calendar, your login, real bookings
u1.asked: Book trips you confirmed, within travel policy
u1.gap: It can act as you, not just book

u2.reach: Your account, invoices and booked travel
u2.asked: Answer questions; trip changes need a person
u2.gap: A help chat can also change trips

u3.reach: Hotel rates from every client's spend
u3.asked: Prepare one client's hotel data and requests
u3.gap: One client's work draws on all clients' data

u1.reach: Every ticket and document you can open
u1.asked: Sort your tickets; keep data inside
u1.gap: Hidden text in a file sent data out

u2.reach: Everything its builder can see and change
u2.asked: Suggest triage notes in one Jira space
u2.gap: It acts as its builder, with nobody approving

u3.reach: Your Atlassian data, sent to other tools
u3.asked: Look up customers; copy nothing out
u3.gap: Data that leaves loses Atlassian's protections

u1.reach: Guest messages, bookings and the property's inbox
u1.asked: Suggest replies; the property approves each one
u1.gap: Unclear what it sends without the property's approval

u2.reach: Your booking, and cancelling it by phone
u2.asked: Cancel only after a clear yes
u2.gap: Unclear how it checks who is calling

u3.reach: Your travel history, prices and one-tap booking
u3.asked: Suggest stays; you confirm every booking
u3.gap: Unclear what reaches the outside AI model

u1.reach: Long prompts in a shared memory pool
u1.asked: Answers built only from your own request
u1.gap: Some answers held other customers' data

u2.reach: The whole Cloudflare API: DNS, security, everything
u2.asked: Add one DNS record for one site
u2.gap: One broad grant opens every product

u3.reach: Logged-in browsers, user accounts and payments
u3.asked: Answer customers; big payments need a person
u3.gap: It can pay unless approval is switched on

u1.reach: Customers' AI agents log in and move money
u1.asked: Pay named bills, up to a limit
u1.gap: Banks can't yet tell good agents from bad

u2.reach: Fraud alerts, rules and suspicious activity reports
u2.asked: Read alerts and draft; people decide
u2.gap: Unclear what it does on its own

u3.reach: Feedzai's data, through the bank's own agents
u3.asked: Read one queue and write notes only
u3.gap: Not yet clear how tightly each is limited

u1.reach: Claim forms, customer messages and reimbursements
u1.asked: Read the form; a person decides
u1.gap: Unclear where a person checks replies

u2.reach: Callers' voices, policy records and call routing
u2.asked: Check the caller, then route the call
u2.gap: Unclear what happens if voice checks fail

u3.reach: Company know-how feeding every other AI system
u3.asked: Answer staff from checked content, with sources
u3.gap: One wrong entry spreads to every AI system

u1.reach: Refunds, disputes and your payment plans, by chat
u1.asked: Routine errands; hard cases go to people
u1.gap: Unclear when hard cases reach a person

u2.reach: Your shopping habits, and buying on credit
u2.asked: Help compare products; you decide to buy
u2.gap: Advice leads straight to buying, maybe on credit

u3.reach: Answers from across Klarna's internal systems
u3.asked: Answer staff only from what they may see
u3.gap: Unclear how it respects each person's access

u1.reach: Web pages, your Gmail and its own server
u1.asked: Summarise the page you chose, nothing else
u1.gap: A page's hidden text could reach your Gmail

u2.reach: Your email and every account you linked
u2.asked: Read email as text; run nothing from it
u2.gap: One email could reach every linked account

u3.reach: Every site you are logged into, as you
u3.gap: Once allowed, it can use every login

u1.reach: All the organisation's email, plus payment keys
u1.asked: Answer questions sent to one address
u1.gap: Its key opens the whole organisation's mail

u2.reach: Every message in the organisation, and sending
u2.asked: Summarise and draft; send only when approved
u2.gap: Nothing in the grant separates draft from send

u3.reach: Its own new inbox, made without a person
u3.asked: Use only the address the operator gave
u3.gap: It can make an inbox nobody knows about

u3.reach: The live database, from the test workspace
u3.gap: The freeze was a request, not a lock

u1.reach: Code, your connected apps and Stripe payments
u1.asked: Test payments only until the owner says go
u1.gap: Connected apps open far more than needed

u2.reach: Databases, secret keys and company data
u2.asked: Build a read-only dashboard; never show secrets
u2.gap: Its connections can write, not just read

u1.reach: The whole mailbox, and sending as you
u1.asked: Find one message and draft; never send
u1.gap: It can send, though it was never asked

u2.reach: Customer records, bulk exports and deals
u2.asked: Export at most 500 contacts, with approval
u2.gap: It can export and delete beyond the limits

u3.reach: The live site, keys and its own transcript
u3.asked: Publish the site; never touch secrets
u3.gap: Keys pasted in chat were within its reach

u1.reach: Web leads, account data and Slack
u1.asked: Help with the newest lead, nothing more
u1.gap: A poisoned web form could steer the agent

u2.asked: Refunds within policy; the rest to people
u2.gap: Each new action widens what it can reach

u3.asked: Big credits wait for a person
u3.gap: It can issue credits before a person looks

u1.reach: Vault keys, and who it hands them to
u1.asked: Seal keys only to the trusted owner
u1.gap: Once delivered, the key sits in plain text

u2.reach: Every file in the shared vault
u2.asked: Work only in its own folder
u2.gap: It can widen its view to any folder

u3.reach: Its inbox, its keys and its own site
u3.asked: Act only on known kinds of request
u3.gap: A verified sender is not always right
